items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: But to play with Count Basie, in that band, because that’s the music that moves my soul.

ctx.x: Speaking of a 30-year-old Wayne, I’m going to go back a little farther than that and create a fictional scenario. If you were 21 or 2, and you got a call to sub on lead trumpet with the Count Basie orchestra on a Sunday, and then you got, unbelievably, a second call to sub on lead trumpet on the Buddy Rich orchestra the next day, what would be the difference in those gigs as far as playing lead trumpet?

Well I would have picked Count Basie’s band and said no to Buddy first of all. Because it’s funny you should mention Count Basie because of any name band that I would have ever wanted to really play — I mean I would have liked to play with any of them. But to play with Count Basie, in that band, because that’s the music that moves my soul. You know I do a lot of other things to make a living but my wife will tell you when I’m playing, you know, a Billy Byers’ chart, or a Frank Foster chart, or a Sammy Nestico…
